title: Defender for Cloud Alerts

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:defender` events with `severity="High" OR severity="Critical"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.9 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:defender` traffic without `severity="High" OR severity="Critical"`. Confirm UC-4.2.9 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:defender` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:defender" severity="High" OR severity="Critical"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.9_defender_for_cloud_alert_9"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.9 — Defender for Cloud Alerts: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:defender` for search criteria `severity="High" OR severity="Critical"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Defender for Cloud Alerts' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.9 drives critical-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Configure Defender for Cloud to export alerts to Event Hub. Ingest via Splunk TA. Alert on High and Critical severity findings.
visualization: Table by severity, Bar chart (alert types), Timeline, Single value (critical count).
knownFalsePositives: A fresh scanner run or a vendor re-rate can resurface a finding we already know about. We deduplicate on resource and time and we only escalate when the exposure is new or the severity stepped up.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:defender`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure Defender for Cloud to export alerts to Event Hub. Ingest via Splunk TA. Alert on High and Critical severity findings.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:defender" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:defender" severity="High" OR severity="Critical"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.9_defender_for_cloud_alert_9"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:defender` in `index=azure` to detect defender for cloud alerts. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_9_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table by severity, Bar chart (alert types), Timeline, Single value (critical count)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of defender for cloud alerts so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
